checks.explanation: DeSantis won re-election as Florida governor in November 2022 with 59.4% of the vote, a nearly 19-point margin over Charlie Crist, the largest margin for a Florida governor's race since 1982. He went on to become a leading (though ultimately unsuccessful) 2024 Republican presidential contender, matching the 'national front-runner' framing of the prediction at the time it was assessed.

sources.title: DeSantis wins 2022 Florida governor's race by largest margin in 40 years

checks.explanation: Stripe did not go public in 2022 or at any point since. Despite 2021 reports of exploring a 2022 direct listing, the company remained private, later running employee tender offers instead of an IPO to relieve liquidity pressure.

sources.title: Stripe Is Discussing Public Listing for 2022 with Bankers (never materialized)

checks.explanation: Democrats lost control of the House in the 2022 midterms, and on November 17, 2022, Nancy Pelosi announced she would not seek re-election to Democratic leadership, stepping down as leader after 20 years while remaining in Congress, closely matching the prediction.

sources.title: Nancy Pelosi to step down as House Democratic leader after two decades

checks.explanation: AOC never launched a 2022 primary challenge against Schumer. She repeatedly declined to rule it out in interviews through 2021 but ultimately did not run, and Schumer was re-elected in 2022 without a serious progressive primary challenge.

sources.title: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez does not rule out 2022 challenge to Chuck Schumer (never materialized)

checks.explanation: The Fed ended its quantitative easing asset-purchase program in March 2022 exactly as predicted, following Powell's January 2022 confirmation of the taper timeline, and followed up with quantitative tightening starting in June 2022.

sources.title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet

checks.explanation: Hispanic and Asian American voters did swing measurably toward Republicans in the 2022 midterms: the Democratic-Republican margin among Hispanic voters shrank by about 26 points versus 2018, and the Asian American margin shrank by about 11 points. The swing was real and matches the prediction's direction, though Democrats still won a majority of both groups overall rather than losing them outright.

sources.title: 2022 US elections: Voting patterns by gender, race, education, age, party, religion

checks.explanation: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022, the deadliest conflict in Europe since WWII, and Taiwan tensions rose sharply in parallel as observers debated whether China would follow Russia's playbook, with a record number of Chinese military flights into Taiwan's air defense zone that year.

sources.title: Will Russia's struggle in Ukraine help Taiwan, or hurt it?

checks.explanation: Putin and Xi issued a 'no limits' partnership declaration on February 4, 2022, just weeks before the Ukraine invasion, and the relationship deepened through the year as China became an economic lifeline for sanctioned Russia, matching the prediction that Putin would grow stronger via closer China ties amid rising US-China tension.

sources.title: China and Russia: Exploring Ties Between Two Authoritarian Powers

checks.explanation: At the 20th Party Congress in October 2022, Xi Jinping secured a precedent-breaking third term, stacked the Politburo Standing Committee entirely with loyalists, and emerged as China's most powerful leader since Mao, exactly matching the 'ruler for life' framing of the prediction.

sources.title: Xi Jinping enters third term as China's most powerful leader in decades surrounded by loyalists

checks.explanation: The midterm-loss part of this prediction was correct (Democrats lost the House), but the more distinctive claim failed: Trump was not 'destroyed' by the January 6 committee to the point of not running again. He announced his 2024 campaign within months and went on to win the presidency, directly contradicting the 'bows out and doesn't run again' prediction.

sources.title: The most likely impact of the Jan. 6 hearings on Trump

checks.explanation: 2022 saw a documented sense of declining US global influence: nearly half of Americans polled said US influence was weakening while two-thirds said China's was strengthening, and February 2022's Putin-Xi 'new era' declaration explicitly challenged US-led global leadership, matching the prediction.

sources.title: U.S. influence in the world declining, many Americans say

checks.explanation: Progressive challengers had a rough 2022: moderate candidates won 14 of 22 competitive primaries where a progressive challenged them, and progressives who did win primaries often lost their general elections, a clear setback for the movement's momentum, matching the prediction.

sources.title: Progressives hoped for big 2022 primary gains, but the results have been mixed

checks.explanation: Small and mid-sized 'enabling layer' businesses did not outperform megacorps in 2022; if anything the opposite occurred. Shopify (the exact company cited as the model 'David' business) crashed roughly 75% in 2022, and smaller, less-profitable growth-stage tech names were generally hit harder than mega-cap tech in the 2022 rate-driven selloff, not less hard.

sources.title: 2022: Big Tech's Year of Reckoning

checks.explanation: The low-tax-state migration trend accelerated exactly as predicted in 2022: Florida gained about 125,551 net income-tax filers and Texas about 88,216, while California lost about 144,203 and New York about 108,586, with a taxpayer moving to Florida or Texas roughly every 4.5 minutes.

sources.title: Americans Moved to Low-Tax States in 2022

checks.explanation: The crypto bubble burst decisively in 2022: the market lost over $2 trillion in value, Terra/Luna collapsed to near-zero in May, FTX collapsed in November, and by October 61% of cryptocurrencies were in negative territory, closely matching the predicted broad-based crypto collapse (the precise '90%' figure isn't independently verifiable but the directional call was strongly correct).

sources.title: Main crypto crashes in 2022: remembering FTX, Celsius Network, Three Arrows Capital, Terra

checks.explanation: The spread trade failed. Visa and Mastercard proved resilient in 2022 (payment volumes stayed strong and neither is dependent on growth multiples the way crypto is), while the 'long web3 crypto projects' side of the trade was disastrous given the confirmed 2022 crypto collapse (market down over $2 trillion, Terra/Luna and FTX both collapsing). Being short Visa/Mastercard and long crypto in 2022 would have lost money on both legs relative to the market, the opposite of the predicted 'most profitable spread trade.'

sources.title: 'Biggest Losers' In 2022 Will Be Visa And MasterCard, Chamath Palihapitiya Says

checks.explanation: China did solidify a nuclear-driven climate leadership position in 2022: it has the world's third-largest nuclear fleet (~52 GW as of September 2022) and accounted for roughly one-third of all nuclear capacity under construction globally at the time, in line with its stated path toward carbon neutrality by 2060, matching the prediction.

sources.title: Nuclear Power in China - World Nuclear Association

checks.explanation: The California school choice/voucher ballot initiative (the Educational Freedom Act, offering roughly $14,000 per pupil) failed to qualify for the 2022 ballot. It needed about 1 million verified signatures and collected only around 200,000, falling far short, so it never became 'the big election in California' as predicted.

sources.title: School choice backers fail to put measure on California's November ballot

checks.explanation: Battery metals had a strong 2022 in a year when most other asset classes fell: lithium carbonate prices surged over 100% year-to-date (reaching a cyclical high in December 2022), nickel rose about 48.6% by Q4, and cobalt hit multi-quarter highs, representing genuine outperformance relative to stocks, bonds, and crypto that year.

sources.title: Charted: The Most Expensive Battery Metals

checks.explanation: The predicted biotech gold rush materialized quickly: Altos Labs launched in January 2022 with $3 billion in funding from backers including Jeff Bezos and Yuri Milner, drew massive mainstream media coverage, and researchers connected to the company reported real breakthroughs in partial Yamanaka-factor cell reprogramming that year, closely matching the prediction.

sources.title: Altos Labs Officially Launches with $3 Billion in Funding to Tackle In Vivo Reprogramming

checks.explanation: The predicted Democratic civil war between progressives and moderates blossomed exactly as described: San Francisco voters recalled progressive DA Chesa Boudin by a 61-39% margin in June 2022, and moderate Mayor London Breed replaced him with a more centrist prosecutor, a high-profile instance of the moderate-vs-progressive split within the party.

sources.title: Chesa Boudin, son of infamous '60s radical, ousted as San Francisco district attorney in recall vote

checks.explanation: 2022 did not see a surge of American economic optimism; it was one of the worst years for market sentiment in over a decade, with the S&P 500 posting its worst year since 2008, inflation hitting roughly 40-year highs, and persistent recession fears dominating the discourse, directly contradicting the predicted exceptionalism-driven boom.

sources.title: 2022: Big Tech's Year of Reckoning
